$comment: Paperclip setup as code (company Line). Read by apply.mjs and github-sync.mjs. Keys starting with $comment are documentation and are never sent. Placeholders in strings: ${repoRoot} ${home} ${key}. SAFETY: every agent is created paused with the timer heartbeat off; apply.mjs never resumes an agent and never enables a heartbeat. To go live the owner resumes ONE agent by hand (README). BUDGETS are Paperclip's to manage (owner decision 2026-09-28): nothing here sets, changes or enforces a budget or budget policy; use the Paperclip UI.

paths.$comment: repoRoot becomes every agent's cwd. It read /home/developer/Desktop/repos/construct (a Linux host) while this checkout is on macOS, so apply.mjs --apply would have repointed all 22 agents at a directory that does not exist and every lane would have failed at startup with 'fatal: not a git repository'. Two approaches are implemented in lib.mjs REPO_ROOT_POLICIES and either can be selected here - swap repoRootPolicy to change which is in force, no code change needed. 'strict-local' (in force) keeps the explicit path below and refuses to apply unless it is a real git checkout on this machine: the value stays visible and reviewable, but each host needs its own edit. 'derive-from-config' ignores the path below and uses the repo this config file lives in: one config then works unchanged on every host, at the cost of the value no longer being stated anywhere. 'trust-config' accepts the path unchecked, for applying to a Paperclip on another host where nothing here can confirm it. Owner picks the default after release; --repo-root-policy overrides per run.

$comment_projects: Each project's workspace is the checkout its runs start from, and Paperclip requires a .git entry directly in it (heartbeat.js hasGitMetadata). Construct: the repo root, which git_worktree agents branch from. Trace's four: also the repo root, because trace/ is untracked in git (.gitignore /trace/) and has no .git of its own; Trace agents run there directly (sharedCheckout) and work in trace/ (their AGENTS.md). github-sync.mjs files mirror issues under the construct project; backlog.mjs files Trace's tasks under theirs.

projects.$comment: The checkout every git_worktree run branches from. Paperclip takes a run's base checkout from the issue's project workspace, never from adapterConfig.cwd: without a project a run falls back to the agent's empty home directory and fails setup with 'fatal: not a git repository'. github-sync.mjs files every mirror issue under this project. A run with no issue (Run now, OG's timer) still has no project and fails the same way.

routines.$comment: Native Paperclip recurring work (GET/POST /api/companies/:id/routines + POST /api/routines/:id/triggers). A routine materializes an auditable execution task on its own schedule, so it survives a run that dies before writing anything - unlike a standing task that re-arms its own check-in, which severs permanently if one run is killed (2026-09-29 outage: the Flow Controller's LIN-121 chain broke on a DNS fault and nothing could wake it again). Created PAUSED, like every agent: the owner activates. Routines are the right primitive for the Flow Controller specifically because a plain heartbeat timer gives a run no $PAPERCLIP_TASK_ID, and its HEARTBEAT.md ends a task-less run immediately.

defaults.$comment_policies: skip_if_active: never stack a second sweep on a slow one. skip_missed: after downtime do NOT replay every missed slot (the 2026-09-29 outage would have enqueued ~10 catch-up runs at once). activityGatePolicy always for the board sweep: its job is to notice the ABSENCE of activity, so gating it on activity would silence it exactly when it is needed - use require_external_activity only for routines that react to work.

items.title: [FLOW] Board sweep
items.$comment: Replaces the self-re-arming check-in on LIN-121. Same 15-minute cadence as agents/flow/HEARTBEAT.md, but the schedule lives in Paperclip instead of in the last run's final write.
items.description:
Run your HEARTBEAT.md board sweep for the Line company.

Clear blockers toward the limit of 3 (oldest first), wake stalled work, wake idle agents with open work, and collect owner decisions. Max 20 cross-task writes per run; spend them on blocked tasks first.

IMPORTANT, confirmed on this board 2026-09-29: a comment alone does NOT wake the assignee of a blocked task. Paperclip does not dispatch blocked tasks, so a comment-only nudge is a no-op (measured: 6 comments, 0 wakes). To actually restart a task you must set a status AND arm executionPolicy.monitor.nextCheckAt, and the task's commentRequired means the status write needs a comment alongside it or it silently reverts.

Entering blocked requires unresolved blockers, a pending interaction/approval, or an unblockDescriptor naming what would unblock it - use that rather than parking work as blocked with no stated remedy.

Never end a run by setting a task to todo: Paperclip does not wake a todo task again after a successful run.

This routine carries its own schedule, so you do NOT need to re-arm a check-in on a standing task to be woken again.
